analysisReport:
Developmental Analysis

Structure

The dual-timeline architecture is the right choice for this story, and the 1968 spine is sound. Two structural items are flagged for our first sessions: the strict one-for-one timeline alternation in chapters nine through fifteen, which twice releases tension the 1968 chapters have earned, and the delayed inciting discovery — the maps do not enter until chapter four.

Flagged for Structure: chapters 1–3 (opening compression), chapters 9–15 (alternation rhythm), chapter 22 (the Aldermoor pivot lands well — protect it as you revise around it).

Characters

Iris is the book's strongest asset and needs almost nothing from us. Marion's want is the central character task: the manuscript knows what she is looking for but not yet why now. Halloran, the surveyor, currently exists to deliver information in three scenes — he deserves either a want of his own or fewer appearances.

Flagged for Characters: Marion's motivation (chapters 2, 6, 11), Halloran's function (chapters 8, 14, 19).

Plot

The mystery mechanics hold under inspection with one exception: the timeline of the annotated coastal map's custody between 1968 and the present has a gap the attentive reader will notice — who held it during the Falmouth years is never accounted for.

Pacing

Scene-level pacing is generally assured. The middle third carries three scenes that do the same job — establishing Marion's isolation — where one would serve. I will propose candidates for consolidation when we reach them chapter by chapter.

Theme

The book knows what it is about — inheritance, and what maps conceal by what they include. The theme is carried well by objects and less well by dialogue; twice, characters state the theme outright where the surrounding scene had already earned it silently.
